current_answer: As of 13 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. OpenAI has declared degraded GPT-6.1 Sol performance in Codex and Work; its latest update at 09:30 AM said mitigation was applied and recovery was being monitored. This is a real service-performance event, but not proof that the model itself became less capable. A detailed account-level complaint includes capacity errors beside an unverified quality claim. A separate controlled report finds intermittent pre-output failures for particular saved reasoning items; that is a narrow request-path issue, not a population quality rate. A 24-task comparison of GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Sol is mixed but cross-sectional. A separate context metadata change is a runtime/context lead, not an observed quality decline. Check the current status and surface; record a local task receipt with task, expected result, model and effort, client, context, route when visible, error or output, correction, artifact, and allowance. Repeat the same task after recovery. Use a fallback only as a separately tracked comparison.

catalogue_card.question: Is GPT-6.1 Sol getting worse, or is the Codex/Work service failing?
catalogue_card.text: OpenAI reports a GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work performance issue and is monitoring recovery. Narrow replay and account reports are serious leads, but broad capability decline remains unproven.

summary: No broad capability decline across popular models is established.
OpenAI reports a specific GPT-6.1 Sol performance issue in Codex and Work; its latest posted update said mitigation was applied and recovery was being monitored.
A detailed account report combines a quality allegation with local capacity errors; a separate controlled report describes intermittent pre-output failures for specific saved reasoning items.
A context metadata report is a separate runtime lead. A 24-task comparison is mixed, cross-sectional, and limited to one repository and one attempt per task.
Check service status, save a local task receipt, and repeat the same task after recovery.
uncertainty: OpenAI status data is aggregate and cannot show whether the incident caused a specific user task result; latest status update checked at 12:10 UTC still said Monitoring and mitigation applied at 09:30 AM.
The severe quality report is one account. Private logs and comparative outputs are not public, so its quality claim cannot be independently scored.
The saved-reasoning replay is a narrow user-provided reproduction with small samples; backend cause and failure rate are unknown.
The context metadata issue is separate; no quality outcome was measured and no connection to the active status incident is established.
The 24-task comparison is one repository with one attempt per task and is not a longitudinal baseline.
Community reports conflict and are self-selected. No denominator, representative sample, or confirmed reader task receipt exists.
The read-only analytics broker was not connected; reader attention, repeat use, outcomes, conversion, and revenue remain unknown.
